column1: # Task ledger — one row per TASK ID declared by a `### Task N:` heading in
# docs/superpowers/plans/. One row per ID, NOT one per heading line: a heading may
# declare two (`### Task 4a / 4b: Workspaces + Invite` owes rows 4a AND 4b). That
# form was invisible to the reader until 2026-09-08 and ten tasks went untracked.
# is re-derived from the plan files on every run and is never hand-typed here; a
# row for a task no plan contains, or a plan task with no row, is a hard failure.
# STATUS VOCABULARY — the done/claimed split is the honest part of this file.
#   done       A merged PR whose title (or the controller record) names THIS plan
#              AND task specifically, and whose merge sha is an ancestor of
#   claimed    Completion asserted only at PLAN or BRANCH granularity — e.g. a PR
#              titled "Plan 1: ..." covering fifteen tasks. The sha is real and is
#              validated the same way, but the per-task mapping is INFERRED and was
#              never audited. Never counted as complete.
#   in-flight  Committed on a branch that has not merged. No sha is recorded,
#              because a branch commit is not an ancestor of main after a squash.
#   todo       Not started, or started and not recorded.
# EVIDENCE IS THE PR'S MERGE COMMIT, NEVER THE IMPLEMENTING COMMIT. This repo
# squash-merges, so the commits that implemented a task are not ancestors of main
# once its PR lands; recording one would false-RED every finished task.
# Status is hand-asserted and machine-validated. It is deliberately NOT derived
# from commit or PR titles: four different formats appear in the merged set
# ("Plan 4 Tasks 6-7", "Plan 3 Chain A (T3-T8)", "Plan 6 T6", "Plan 2:"), and this
# repo has already recorded that commit messages are not a reliable completion
# signal. Where a title was the only evidence, the row is `claimed`, not `done`.
